title: Finite homogeneous generators of a finitely generated graded module
statement: Let k be a field and S=k[x_0,x_1], graded by total degree (S_d is the k-span of monomials of total degree d, and S_d=0 for d<0), with the projective-line convention [def-sc-p1-standard]. Every finitely generated Z-graded S-module M has a finite homogeneous generating set m_1,...,m_r; consequently the graded map F_0=direct sum_{j=1}^r S(-deg m_j) \to M (S(e) the shifted graded module [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (2)) sending the j-th basis vector to m_j is a surjective graded S-linear map.

source.place: proof, construction of the initial graded free module from homogeneous generators

proof.text: Choose ordinary S-module generators a_1,...,a_t of M. Since M is a direct sum of its graded pieces, each a_i has a finite expansion a_i=\sum_d a_{i,d} with a_{i,d} in M_d. Collect these finitely many homogeneous components. Every a_i is in their S-span, so that span contains the given generators and equals M (including the case M=0, when the collection can be empty).

source.place: proof, construction of F_0 from finitely many homogeneous generators of M; elementary expansion of ordinary generators

proof.text: List the components from step 1 as homogeneous generators m_j of degree d_j. By the shift convention [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] (2), the basis vector 1 in S(-d_j) has degree d_j. Thus s in its degree-n piece is a polynomial of degree n-d_j, and s m_j lies in M_n. The maps S(-d_j) \to M given by s \mapsto s m_j are therefore graded and S-linear; their finite direct sum is the displayed graded map F_0 \to M.

source.place: proof, construction of the initial graded free module from homogeneous generators

proof.text: The image of F_0 \to M is the S-span of the m_j, which is M by step 1. Hence the graded map is surjective.
